Intuitive eating is associated with fewer eating disorder symptoms and body image concerns than flexible control and rigid control, and this is mediated by body appreciation.

rigid dietary control was associated with higher levels of all outcome variables, flexible control was associated with lower levels of disorded eating and body image, and intuitive eating was associated with lower disordered eating and lower levels of body image.

the role of dietary control in the etiology and maintenance of eating disorders and related concerns, and the role of intuitive eating in promoting positive outcomes.

intuitive eating and body appreciation are protective of disordered eating, and body appreciation is protective of body image concerns.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intuitive eating is the most adaptive dietary approach to food and eating and that it is associated with lower disordered eating and better body image.
intuitive eating may be a more effective approach to promoting positive body image and reducing the likelihood of disordered eating than rigid and flexible control.
rigid control is the most maladaptive of all dietary control styles.

it is possible to eat intuitively without engaging in rigid dietary control.
the promotion of intuitive eating may be beneficial for the prevention of eating disorders.
intuitive eating is an important target in eating disorder prevention and treatment efforts.
